title: Pseudo-coherence is closed under distinguished triangles
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let A \to B \to C \to A[1] be a distinguished triangle in D(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If A and C are pseudo-coherent objects [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], then B is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, section Pseudo-coherent modules, Tag 08CD (label lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent), part (2) applied for every m

proof.text: For each point y choose finite-free bounded-above models PA and PC on neighbourhoods UA and UC using IsPseudoCoherent. Take an affine U contained in UA intersect UC and containing y. The private helper restrict_finiteFree_model applies overMap to each complex. Its zero-object preservation preserves the upper bound; mapFreeIso and overMapUnitIso preserve finite free terms. mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, overFunctorMap and mapDerivedCategoryFactors compose the comparison isomorphisms. This gives models A and C for the restricted first and third objects.

The private helper affine_finiteFree_module_model constructs its module complex explicitly by applying affine global sections termwise after transporting through the over equivalence and the affine spectrum isomorphism. For each finite-free term, tildeFinsupp and mapFreeIso exhibit it as the sheafification of a finite free module. Full faithfulness of the affine tilde/Gamma adjunction makes its counit an isomorphism on these terms. The counit is natural in the differentials, giving a complex isomorphism from the sheafified sections complex to the original complex. Sections preserve its zero terms and carry its finite-free isomorphisms to projective modules. The sections complex is bounded above and projective in each degree, so it is K-projective.

Apply affine_localized_derived_sheafification to obtain a full functor G and its natural comparison Q followed by G isomorphic to termwise sheafification followed by Q. Conjugate a derived arrow between the two finite-free models by their counit comparisons, take its preimage under G, and use K-projectivity to represent this preimage by a module chain map. Sheafification and conjugation by the complex counits give a sheaf chain map. Naturality of the comparison, the fullness equation and iso cancellation show that Q of this chain map equals the given derived arrow. This is the proved private helper affine_finiteFree_map_representative.

Derived restriction preserves the distinguished triangle. Inverse-rotate it to C[-1] -> A -> B -> C. Shift the C model using shiftFunctorObjXIso and Q.commShiftIso; it is still bounded above and finite free. Apply the preceding chain-map representative helper to the conjugated first arrow, obtaining g:Cmodel[-1]->Amodel with Q(g) equal to that arrow. Compare Q of the mapping-cone triangle with the inverse rotation using exists_iso_of_arrow_iso and the two model isomorphisms. Their third components identify the restricted B with Q(cone(g)).

The private helper finiteFree_mappingCone uses the cone degree isomorphism with Cmodel[i] biproduct Amodel[i]. mappingCone.isZero_X_iff and the shift degree isomorphism show that these terms vanish above the maximum of the two bounds. Map the finite-free term isomorphisms through biprod.mapIso, then use biprod.isoCoprod, freeSumIso and the free functor applied to the finite-basis reindexing to obtain rank a+b. The resulting bounded-above finite-free model and the comparison from the previous step supply every field of IsPseudoCoherent at y.
